description: A song-form sequencer: a chain of eight phrases, each with its own length in bars, key and tempo, and each deciding which of four instrument clock buses are playing

params.text: Returns the arrangement to the first active phrase on each press
Sets that phrase's scale; it is ignored while that phrase's scale link is on
Sets that phrase's root note; it is ignored while that phrase's root link is on
Sets that phrase's tempo, 30 to 300 beats per minute; it is ignored while that phrase's tempo link is on
Divides the master clock for that channel by 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 or 16, re-aligning to the bar
Links that phrase's scale to the phrase before it, so it inherits the group leader's scale exactly and its own trimmer does nothing
Links that phrase's root to the phrase before it, so it inherits the group leader's root exactly and its own trimmer does nothing
Links that phrase's tempo to the phrase before it, so it inherits the group leader's tempo exactly and its own trimmer does nothing

inputs.text: Each rise counts one bar and advances the arrangement once the phrase has had its length
The master clock that each of the four channels divides down
A rise returns the arrangement to the first active phrase

outputs.text: Which phrase is playing, one volt per phrase with the first at 0V
The tempo of the playing phrase at a hundredth of a volt per beat per minute, for a Meter set to read its tempo CV absolutely
The root of the playing phrase as a volt per octave snapped to semitones, for driving the root input of a sequencer
The scale of the playing phrase at one volt per scale, for driving the scale input of a sequencer
One pulse per bar for that channel, silenced on any phrase where that channel is switched off
The master clock divided by that channel's division, silenced on any phrase where that channel is switched off
A trigger on a master reset and again whenever that channel is switched back on, so an instrument re-enters in step rather than mid-pattern
A trigger when the arrangement wraps round to its first phrase
Carries 10V for as long as that phrase is playing

notes: the module has no clock of its own: it counts the bar pulses coming in and hands out divided, gated copies of the clock coming in
the phrase lengths, which phrases are active and which channels play in each are all set on the display, which cannot be reached by clicking for help
the link dots come up on, so one key and one tempo run through the whole song until a link is broken; a broken link starts a new group the phrases after it inherit from
menu: Trimpots = scale / root / BPM · LEDs link each row independently (linked = inherit) — a label saying what the trimmers and the link dots do
Grid = bars · colored bars = channel enables · dbl-click phrase = on/off — a label saying what the mouse does on the display

outputs.2: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
